session_covered: US and European sessions of Tuesday 6 October
intro: Covers the US session of Tuesday 6 October. Sourcing caveat: the AFR column was not accessible, final closes differ slightly between sources, and no verified Wednesday SPI 200 print was found; unresolved items are marked "not available".
footnotes: S&P 500: approximate figure (the email gave "c.7,825 pts +0.67%").
NASDAQ Composite: the email gave "c.27,646 pts c.+0.6% to +0.8%", which isn't a single figure, so it isn't shown in full.
Dow Jones Industrial Average: the email gave "c.51,523 pts c.+0.5% to +0.7%", which isn't a single figure, so it isn't shown in full.
US 10-year Treasury yield: the email gave "c.5.27% c.-4 to -5 bp", which isn't a single figure, so it isn't shown in full.

Index figures are late-session snapshots that differ across Yahoo Finance, TheStreet, FXEmpire and Trading Economics (Nasdaq +0.61% to +0.83%, Dow +0.50% to +0.70%); S&P 500 +0.67% is confirmed by two sources. Brent: sources conflict (US$98.67/bbl, -1.6% vs US$100.82/bbl, +0.5%), so not reported. Gold: Trading Economics shows US$4,175.36 (+0.86%). AUD/USD and iron ore are from ABC's Tuesday Sydney-session wrap. VIX print could not be date-verified.

setup.summary: SPI 200 / ASX 200 futures for this morning: not available (no two independent verified prints). The overnight US risk tone was positive (record S&P 500 and Nasdaq, lower yields), which is consistent with a firmer open, but it is not quantified here. The ASX 200 closed Tuesday at about 8,733-8,736, +0.5% to +0.6%, a third straight gain.

what_moved: Tech led again as US Treasury yields retreated from 24-year highs (the 10-year touched above 5.35% on Monday), easing rate pressure, while crude dipped on Hormuz supply relief. Small caps lagged (Russell 2000 lower, healthcare weak). S&P 500 sector percentages were not reported in the sources accessed.

news.headline: Yields ease from multi-decade highs.
news.summary: The 10-year was around 5.26-5.28% and the 30-year about 5.65%, after Monday's highest levels since 2002.

news.headline: Oil slips on supply signals.
news.summary: A G7 emergency stockpile release and resilient Middle East exports weighed, and tanker traffic through Hormuz improved.

news.headline: Fed minutes due Wednesday.
news.summary: The September meeting minutes are out at 2pm ET; markets price about 20% odds of an October hike and about 70% for December (Trading Economics).

news.headline: AI trade extends.
news.summary: Constellation Energy rose about 14% on a Google nuclear power deal, and AMD's CEO said compute demand continues to outrun supply.

news.headline: Breadth remains narrow.
news.summary: The Nasdaq logged more than twice as many new 52-week lows as highs despite the record close.

news.headline: Euro weak on French fiscal worries.
news.summary: The euro sits near 17-month lows, and the Australian dollar hit a 22-month high against it (62.1 euro cents).

news.headline: Australian consumer confidence falls.
news.summary: Westpac's index dropped 4.7% to 80.4 on fuel and borrowing costs.

news.headline: US earnings season starts next week.
news.summary: FactSet growth estimates are near 30%, with high expectations already priced in.

coming_up: Fed September meeting minutes: Wednesday 7 October, 2pm ET (05:00 Thursday 8 October AEDT). US Q3 earnings season begins next week.
